title: constexpr and Compile-Time Computation
learningObjectives: Explain the main ideas of constexpr and Compile-Time Computation.
Identify the language rules and relevant C++ constructs.
Apply the topic in a small program.
Recognize common pitfalls and safety concerns.
Test an example and justify design decisions.

understand.concept: constexpr permits compile-time evaluation when expression rules allow. constexpr functions can also run at runtime. static_assert verifies compile-time conditions.
understand.whyItMatters: Compile-time calculations and checks can catch constraints early and express fixed values.
understand.explain: Use constexpr for simple stable calculations and static_assert for compile-time checks; don't force complexity into compile-time code.

examples.title: Core demonstration
examples.code:
constexpr int square(int n){return n*n;}
int main(){constexpr int v=square(5);static_assert(v==25);}
examples.explanation: Use constexpr for simple stable calculations and static_assert for compile-time checks; don't force complexity into compile-time code.

examples.title: Practical example
examples.code:
constexpr int triple(int n){return n*3;}
int main(){int runtime=4;return triple(runtime)==12?0:1;}
examples.explanation: Use constexpr for simple stable calculations and static_assert for compile-time checks; don't force complexity into compile-time code.
